input.question: What was popular British opinion of the American Revolution?
input.ground_truth: Something that could be used to gauge popular opinion in that time was voting in the House of Commons. The last time any PM was defeated over issue of war and peace (until David Cameron on Syria) was in 1782 regarding the rebellious American colonies.

Okay! Imagine you have a big family. Some people in your family live far away, like in another country. Now, let’s say the people living far away decide they don’t want to listen to some of the rules from your family anymore, and they want to make their own rules. 

Some people in your own home (Britain) might think, “Hey, they’re our family! We should help them or tell them what to do.” But other people might not care as much, or even be mad because they think the far-away family is being naughty for leaving.

So, when the American Revolution happened, some people in Britain thought the Americans were wrong for leaving, and some people didn’t really care, or even thought it was a bad idea for Britain to try to stop them. But a lot of people in Britain thought the Americans should still listen to the King and stay part of the family.
